TECHNICAL
WHAT: On macOS, hiding the dock icon requires switching NSApplication activation policy to Accessory. Tauri's `AppHandle::set_activation_policy()` goes through the runtime event loop and silently fails in practice.
WHERE: `src-tauri/src/platform/macos.rs` — `set_dock_icon_visible(visible: bool)` function
HOW: Direct Cocoa FFI via `objc` crate:
```rust
#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
pub(crate) fn set_dock_icon_visible(visible: bool) {
    use objc::runtime::Object;
    unsafe {
        let cls = objc::class!(NSApplication);
        let app: *mut Object = msg_send![cls, sharedApplication];
        let policy = if visible { 0i64 } else { 1i64 }; // Regular=0, Accessory=1
        let _: () = msg_send![app, setActivationPolicy: policy];
    }
}
```
WHY: Tauri's wrapper sends a message to the runtime event loop which may not execute synchronously or reliably during app state transitions
GOTCHA: Must dispatch on main thread. After switching to Accessory policy, macOS steals focus — call `window.set_focus()` immediately after to keep Whisnap focused
